claims.claim: Head-to-head, no organization structure wins outright: graph/structured retrieval wins multi-hop reasoning + global/contextual sense-making + synthesis-into-narrative; FLAT top-k matches or beats it on isolated fact retrieval (basic RAG 83.2% evidence recall on single-passage), because graph processing injects redundant/noisy info on simple queries. Task-shape is the deciding variable, not a universal 'structure is better'.
claims.source: When Do We Need Graph Structures in RAG? (arXiv 2506.05690v3, 2025)
claims.relevance: Directly answers the brief's 'which structures win on what task shapes' — tells us structure only pays off if our workload is multi-hop/aggregation, not single-fact lookup.

claims.claim: HippoRAG 2 (open KG of phrase-nodes + passage-nodes, retrieved by Personalized PageRank) beats dense-flat NV-Embed-v2 on multi-hop (2Wiki 71.0 vs 61.5 F1; Recall@5 2Wiki 76.5->90.4, MuSiQue 69.7->74.7, HotpotQA 94.5->96.3) WITHOUT hurting simple QA (NQ 63.3 vs 61.9 F1); avg 59.8 vs 57.0 F1. Key design: the KG AIDS retrieval, it does not replace/expand the corpus.
claims.source: From RAG to Memory: Non-Parametric Continual Learning for LLMs / HippoRAG 2 (arXiv 2502.14802v1, 2025)
claims.relevance: The cleanest measured 'graph-aids-retrieval beats flat without single-hop regression' result; PPR-over-KG is a value-org candidate whose win is attributable and whose build cost is bounded.

claims.claim: Build-cost ordering is dramatic and is the real constraint: HippoRAG 2 indexes MuSiQue (11,656 passages) with 9.2M input tokens vs LightRAG 68.5M vs GraphRAG 115.5M. Restated by the survey as per-query token overhead MS-GraphRAG up to 4x10^4, LightRAG ~10^4, HippoRAG2 ~10^3. LightRAG scored only 6.6 F1 avg in HippoRAG2's eval — LLM-generated graph noise can actively hurt when the KG expands the corpus.
claims.source: HippoRAG 2 (arXiv 2502.14802) + When Do We Need Graph Structures in RAG (arXiv 2506.05690)
claims.relevance: Sets the cost axis for our grid: community-summary graphs are ~10-100x the index cost and can degrade quality; PPR-over-open-KG is the low-cost structured option.

claims.claim: RAPTOR (recursive cluster+summarize into a bottom-up tree, retrieval at multiple abstraction levels) is the foundational hierarchical baseline: +20% absolute accuracy on QuALITY when coupled with GPT-4. It integrates knowledge by SIMILARITY only (later criticized as its limitation).
claims.source: RAPTOR: Recursive Abstractive Processing for Tree-Organized Retrieval (arXiv 2401.18059, ICLR 2024)
claims.relevance: The reference point every 2025-26 tree/hierarchy successor measures against; the similarity-only limitation motivates SiReRAG/graph hybrids.

claims.claim: LeanRAG = semantic-aggregation (cluster entities + build explicit cross-cluster relations) + bottom-up structure-guided retrieval over a KG; reduces retrieval redundancy by 46% and outperforms prior methods on 4 QA benchmarks. Explicitly fixes two GraphRAG failure modes: 'semantic islands' (disconnected community summaries) and retrieval degenerating into flat search that ignores graph topology.
claims.source: LeanRAG: Knowledge-Graph-Based Generation with Semantic Aggregation and Hierarchical Retrieval (arXiv 2508.10391, 2025)
claims.relevance: Names the two concrete pathologies a hierarchical-KG value-org must avoid, and quantifies the redundancy win — a design spec if we go structured.

claims.claim: UniversalRAG routes retrieval across BOTH modality (text/image/video) AND granularity (paragraph vs document; clip vs full video) via a learned router, beating single-modality/single-granularity flat RAG on text (NQ/HotpotQA), multimodal (WebQA/InfoSeek) and video (VideoRAG) benchmarks. Critically: it covers text/image/video only — NO audio/speech modality.
claims.source: UniversalRAG: RAG over Corpora of Diverse Modalities and Granularities (arXiv 2504.20734, 2025)
claims.relevance: Closest analog to our modality+grain-tagged design and proof that granularity-routing beats flat — but the explicit absence of speech is a gap our system would be first to fill.

claims.claim: Recursive summarization amplifies hallucination: hierarchical merging propagates fabrications up the tree; replacing/aligning intermediate summaries with source-document context beats plain hierarchical merging (Llama-3.1 family, legal+narrative domains).
claims.source: Context-Aware Hierarchical Merging for Long Document Summarization, Ou & Lapata (arXiv 2502.00977, ACL Findings 2025) — not opened (search snippet + abstract listing)
claims.relevance: Load-bearing caution against RAPTOR-style summary-node value-org: the summary nodes themselves can be the error source; a mitigation (keep source context) is known.

claims.claim: NodeRAG (heterogeneous-node graph) reports 89% on MuSiQue with only ~5,000 retrieval tokens, beating GraphRAG/LightRAG on indexing time, query time, storage AND multi-hop QA with minimal retrieval tokens.
claims.source: NodeRAG: Structuring Graph-based RAG with Heterogeneous Nodes (arXiv 2504.11544, 2025) — not opened (search snippet)
claims.relevance: A 2025 graph successor that pushes the token-cost frontier down further than HippoRAG2 while keeping multi-hop wins.

claims.claim: PathRAG adds a flow-control pruning mechanism on top of a LightRAG-style index: keyword-anchored candidate entities/relations, then prune to the most relevant PATHS — cutting redundant graph context at retrieval time (a retrieval-strategy overlay on any KG org).
claims.source: PathRAG (search snippet via NodeRAG/E2GraphRAG survey results, 2025) — not opened
claims.relevance: Shows organization and retrieval-strategy are separable; path-pruning is a cheap add-on to reduce graph-RAG's redundancy.

claims.claim: Parent-child / hierarchical multi-granularity stores decouple retrieval granularity from generation context: index & match on small CHILD chunks (precision) but return the larger PARENT chunk (coherent generation input). Requires NO LLM at build time — just a chunk hierarchy + child embeddings.
claims.source: H-RAG (arXiv 2605.00631, SemEval-2026 Task 8) + LangChain ParentDocumentRetriever docs — not opened (search snippets)
claims.relevance: Lowest-cost structured upgrade over flat: child-key -> parent-value is implementable on faiss with zero extra LLM calls, directly compatible with our speech-vector keys.

claims.claim: Mix-of-Granularity learns to route the CHUNK granularity per query (soft mixture over granularity levels) rather than fixing one chunk size.
claims.source: Mix-of-Granularity: Optimize the Chunking Granularity for RAG (arXiv 2406.00456, 2024) — not opened (search snippet)
claims.relevance: A learned granularity-selector — a query-construction/retrieval-strategy lever adjacent to our later RL controller.

claims.claim: SiReRAG indexes BOTH similarity AND relatedness (entity relations), explicitly to fix RAPTOR's similarity-only integration, targeting multi-hop reasoning.
claims.source: SiReRAG: Indexing Similar and Related Information for Multihop Reasoning (arXiv 2412.06206, 2024/2025) — not opened (search snippet)
claims.relevance: Hybrid tree+relatedness value-org; the 'add a relatedness axis to a similarity index' move is cheap and directly grafts onto a faiss store.

claims.claim: The agent-memory field converged in 2025-26 on a three-tier grain taxonomy — episodic / semantic / procedural — mirroring cognitive science; frameworks differ mainly in how each tier is stored and how the episodic<->semantic consolidation policy is implemented.
claims.source: State of AI Agent Memory 2026 (mem0.ai blog) + surveys: Rethinking Memory Mechanisms of Foundation Agents (arXiv 2602.06052) + Anatomy of Agentic Memory (arXiv 2602.19320) — not opened (search snippets)
claims.relevance: External validation that our grain-tagged (knowledge/memory/exemplar) value-org matches the field's converged taxonomy; positions us against mem0/MemGPT.

claims.claim: A-MEM organizes memory as a self-linking Zettelkasten note network: each note = content + LLM-generated keywords/tags/context; a new note triggers the LLM to REWRITE the context/attributes of its linked neighbors (organic write-back), yielding strong multi-hop reasoning — a structurally richer episodic store than mem0's flat ADD/UPDATE/DELETE/NOOP facts.
claims.source: A-Mem: Agentic Memory for LLM Agents (arXiv 2502.12110, NeurIPS 2025) — not opened (search snippet + OpenReview)
claims.relevance: Positions a newer episodic store against the known mem0/MemGPT line; the neighbor-rewrite is a concrete write-back policy candidate for our memory grain.

claims.claim: Zep/Graphiti = bi-temporal knowledge-graph memory with episodic + semantic + community subgraphs; non-lossy updates with validity intervals. DMR 94.8% (> MemGPT 93.4%); LongMemEval up to +18.5% accuracy and -90% latency on complex temporal reasoning.
claims.source: Zep: A Temporal Knowledge Graph Architecture for Agent Memory (arXiv 2501.13956, 2025) — not opened (search snippet + emergentmind/blog)
claims.relevance: Newer than MemGPT (which is in our records) and beats it; a temporal-KG value-org for the memory grain with hierarchical subgraphs = the schema-first structured store option.

claims.claim: Write-back / consolidation is an active 2026 design surface: AutoDream (Feb 2026) runs a background sub-agent that reviews+consolidates memory files during idle time (REM-sleep analogy); TRUSTMEM and self-consolidation work add trustworthy/learned consolidation policies; SAGE adds a novelty gate to decide what to write.
claims.source: AI Agent Memory Architectures (zylos.ai, 2026-04) + TRUSTMEM (arXiv 2606.25161) + Self-Consolidation for Self-Evolving Agents (arXiv 2602.01966) + SAGE (arXiv 2605.30711) — not opened (search snippets)
claims.relevance: The consolidation/write-back policy is the natural home for our later training-free RL lever (what to store, when to compress) — currently all heuristic/LLM-prompted, none RL-optimized.

claims.claim: ReasoningBank distills reusable strategies/reasoning hints from past trajectories into STRUCTURED memory items (not raw traces, which are too long/noisy) for self-evolving agents; CBR-for-LLM formalizes retrieve-reuse-revise-retain with memory banks of (question, chain-of-thought, answer) exemplar triples.
claims.source: ReasoningBank (arXiv 2509.25140, 2025) + Review of Case-Based Reasoning for LLM Agents (arXiv 2504.06943, 2025) — not opened (search snippets)
claims.relevance: The organization form for our EXEMPLAR grain: store distilled cases, not raw episodes; retrieval + reuse + retention is the write-back loop for exemplars.

claims.claim: GraphRAG is NOT uniformly better: reported -13.4% accuracy on Natural Questions vs vanilla RAG and -16.6% on time-sensitive/real-time-update questions; graph retrieval also carries ~2.3x higher latency on HotpotQA for a ~4.5% reasoning gain.
claims.source: Multiple 2025 GraphRAG-vs-RAG analyses (atlan.com knowledge-graph-vs-rag; When-to-use-Graphs survey) — partially opened (survey 2506.05690 opened; specific NQ/time-sensitive numbers from search snippet, not opened)
claims.relevance: Guards against over-adopting graph org for freshness-sensitive or single-hop parts of our workload; latency cost matters for a local llama.cpp serving loop.

claims.claim: Multimodal instantiations of graph org exist for text+image+video: M3KG-RAG builds a multi-hop MULTIMODAL KG for modality-wise retrieval; MegaRAG is a multimodal-KG RAG; MDKAG builds a disciplinary MMKG from textbooks/slides/videos and uses hierarchical clustering when entity types exceed 50. Video is handled via ASR-timestamped transcription (i.e., audio is transcribed, not natively keyed).
claims.source: M3KG-RAG (arXiv 2512.20136) + MegaRAG (arXiv 2512.20626) + MDKAG (MDPI Applied Sciences 15/16/9095, 2025) — not opened (search snippets)
claims.relevance: Confirms multimodal graph/hierarchy org is being built, but audio enters only via ASR transcription — nobody keys the graph on native acoustic vectors, which is our differentiator.

claims.claim: Hierarchical/graph org trades offline build cost for online retrieval cost: HiRAG reports higher offline indexing cost but ~zero online token retrieval cost; ArchRAG emphasizes lower online token cost than graph baselines. Concretely, indexing 800KB with GPT-4.1 ~ $10-15 (>90% cheaper with mini/Flash); LightRAG consumed 757M tokens on HotpotQA vs 62M for naive RAG.
claims.source: The Hidden Cost of 98% Accuracy (Tao An, Medium 2025/26) + RAGFlow 2025 year-end review — not opened (search snippets)
claims.relevance: For our LOCAL llama.cpp 30B, the offline build (LLM summarization/triple-extraction) is the binding cost; these numbers assume API GPT-4-class, so our wall-clock build cost is likely worse and must be measured.

claims.claim: Speech-native RAG stores today are text-audio HYBRID keyed on transcribed/audio-adapter embeddings (WavRAG's WavRetriever over a text-audio KB, 10x speedup vs ASR-Text cascade), and newer PlanRAG-Audio adds plan-then-retrieve structure for long-form audio understanding — but none impose a hierarchical/graph ORGANIZATION over the audio store; they remain flat hybrid indexes.
claims.source: WavRAG (ACL 2025 Long 613 / arXiv 2502.14727) [known prior art] + PlanRAG-Audio (arXiv 2605.20414) — not opened (search snippets)
claims.relevance: Confirms the Dimension-2 gap for our track: speech RAG has flat hybrid stores only; hierarchical/graph/grain-tagged organization over speech-vector keys is unclaimed territory.

claims.claim: DTCRS (Dynamic Tree Construction for Recursive Summarization) targets RAPTOR's redundancy: recursive summarization introduces many summaries unrelated to the answer, so it builds the tree dynamically to cut redundant summaries.
claims.source: DTCRS: Dynamic Tree Construction for Recursive Summarization (arXiv 2604.07012, 2026) — not opened (search snippet)
claims.relevance: A 2026 RAPTOR successor confirming redundant summary nodes are the tree's main weakness — reinforces LeanRAG's redundancy-reduction motivation.

claims.claim: Cross-granularity hypergraph RAG and structure-aware on-demand hypergraph memory push graph org toward hyper-edges for multi-hop QA / long-document QA, incorporating richer graph structures than pairwise KG.
claims.source: Cross-Granularity Hypergraph RAG for Multi-hop QA (arXiv 2508.11247) + Structure-Aware On-Demand Hypergraph Memory (arXiv 2606.10921) — not opened (search snippets)
claims.relevance: Frontier value-org (hyperedges); high build cost, likely out of budget for our stack but worth logging as an upper bound on structural richness.

candidates.name: Flat passage/chunk store (baseline)
candidates.what: Single-level faiss index of utterance/word-keyed value chunks, retrieved by top-k similarity. Our current mock. Wins single-hop/fact lookup; loses multi-hop/aggregation.
candidates.evidence: When-to-use-Graphs (2506.05690, opened): flat basic RAG 83.2% evidence recall on single-passage facts, matches/beats structure there.

candidates.name: Grain-tagged hybrid store (current design)
candidates.what: One store, values tagged knowledge/memory/exemplar (three-tier taxonomy), routed by tag at retrieval. Already implemented.
candidates.evidence: 2025-26 agent-memory field converged on episodic/semantic/procedural grain taxonomy (mem0 State-of-2026; surveys 2602.06052, 2602.19320 — not opened). Validates the design but head-to-head grain-vs-flat measurement is missing.

candidates.name: Parent-child multi-granularity store
candidates.what: Index/match on small child chunks (child = faiss key), return the larger parent chunk as the value delivered to the omni model. Decouples retrieval precision from generation coherence. No LLM at build.
candidates.evidence: H-RAG (2605.00631) + LangChain ParentDocumentRetriever (not opened); design rationale = fine chunks retrieve, coarse chunks generate.

candidates.name: RAPTOR recursive summary tree
candidates.what: Recursively cluster + LLM-summarize value chunks into a bottom-up tree; retrieve at multiple abstraction levels (leaf detail + node gist).
candidates.evidence: RAPTOR (2401.18059, opened): +20% absolute on QuALITY with GPT-4. Caution: summary nodes amplify hallucination (Ou & Lapata 2502.00977, not opened).

candidates.name: SiReRAG (similarity + relatedness dual index)
candidates.what: Augment the similarity tree/index with a relatedness (entity-relation) axis, fixing RAPTOR's similarity-only integration for multi-hop.
candidates.evidence: SiReRAG (2412.06206, not opened): dual-axis indexing for multihop reasoning.

candidates.name: Open-KG + Personalized PageRank (HippoRAG-2 style)
candidates.what: Build an open KG of phrase-nodes + passage-nodes from LLM-extracted triples; retrieve by PPR seeded on query. KG AIDS retrieval, does not replace the corpus.
candidates.evidence: HippoRAG 2 (2502.14802, opened): multi-hop 2Wiki 71.0 vs 61.5 F1, Recall@5 76.5->90.4, no single-hop regression, index 9.2M vs GraphRAG 115.5M tokens.

candidates.name: LeanRAG semantic-aggregation hierarchical KG
candidates.what: Cluster entities + build explicit cross-cluster relations (kill 'semantic islands'), then bottom-up structure-guided retrieval anchored to fine entities.
candidates.evidence: LeanRAG (2508.10391, opened): -46% retrieval redundancy, beats prior on 4 QA benchmarks.

candidates.name: MS GraphRAG community-summary graph
candidates.what: Entity KG + pregenerated community summaries; map-reduce partial answers for global/aggregation queries.
candidates.evidence: GraphRAG (2404.16130, search-confirmed): substantial comprehensiveness/diversity gains on 1M-token global sense-making. But astronomical build cost (up to 4x10^4 tokens/query; 757M-token indexing) and -13.4% on NQ.

candidates.name: NodeRAG heterogeneous-node graph
candidates.what: Graph with typed heterogeneous nodes for better context propagation; minimal retrieval tokens.
candidates.evidence: NodeRAG (2504.11544, not opened): 89% MuSiQue at ~5,000 retrieval tokens, beats GraphRAG/LightRAG on index+query time+storage.

candidates.name: PathRAG flow-control path pruning
candidates.what: Retrieval-time overlay on any KG: keyword-anchor candidates, then prune to most-relevant paths to cut redundant graph context. Org-agnostic.
candidates.evidence: PathRAG (search snippet, not opened): flow-control pruning over LightRAG-style index.

candidates.name: Zep/Graphiti bi-temporal KG memory
candidates.what: Temporal KG with episodic+semantic+community subgraphs, non-lossy updates with validity intervals — schema-first structured store for the memory grain.
candidates.evidence: Zep (2501.13956, not opened): DMR 94.8% > MemGPT 93.4%; LongMemEval +18.5% acc, -90% latency.

candidates.name: A-MEM Zettelkasten self-linking notes
candidates.what: Episodic notes (content + LLM keywords/tags/context) auto-linked; new note triggers LLM rewrite of linked neighbors (organic write-back).
candidates.evidence: A-Mem (2502.12110, NeurIPS 2025, not opened): stronger multi-hop than flat mem0 ADD/UPDATE/DELETE/NOOP facts.

candidates.name: Episodic bank + consolidation/write-back policy
candidates.what: Memory-grain bank with a policy for what to store, when to compress episodic->semantic, and what to retire (novelty gate / idle consolidation).
candidates.evidence: AutoDream idle consolidation (zylos, not opened), SAGE novelty gate (2605.30711), TRUSTMEM (2606.25161) — all heuristic/LLM-prompted, none RL-optimized: the natural home for our training-free RL lever.

candidates.name: ReasoningBank / CBR exemplar bank
candidates.what: Store DISTILLED cases/strategies (not raw traces) as exemplar-grain values; retrieve-reuse-revise-retain loop.
candidates.evidence: ReasoningBank (2509.25140) + CBR-for-LLM review (2504.06943), not opened: distilled (Q,CoT,A)/strategy items outperform raw-trajectory memory.

candidates.name: UniversalRAG modality+granularity router
candidates.what: A router that picks BOTH modality and granularity (paragraph/document, clip/video) per query before retrieval.
candidates.evidence: UniversalRAG (2504.20734, opened): beats single-modality/single-granularity flat RAG; but NO audio modality — we'd extend to speech.

candidates.name: Mix-of-Granularity learned chunk router
candidates.what: Soft learned mixture over chunk-granularity levels per query, instead of one fixed chunk size.
candidates.evidence: Mix-of-Granularity (2406.00456, not opened): learns granularity per query.

candidates.name: Multimodal KG (M3KG-RAG / MegaRAG)
candidates.what: Multi-hop multimodal knowledge graph over text+image+video (audio only via ASR transcription).
candidates.evidence: M3KG-RAG (2512.20136), MegaRAG (2512.20626), MDKAG (MDPI 2025), not opened: modality-wise KG retrieval; none key on native acoustic vectors.

candidates.name: Cross-granularity hypergraph store
candidates.what: Hyperedges linking multi-granularity units for multi-hop / long-document QA — richer than pairwise KG.
candidates.evidence: Cross-Granularity Hypergraph RAG (2508.11247) + on-demand hypergraph memory (2606.10921), not opened.

gaps:
EXPLICIT GAPS (Dimension 2, positioned against our frozen-omni + speech-vector-keyed faiss KB):

1. NOBODY organizes over speech-vector keys. Every measured structural win (RAPTOR, HippoRAG-2, LeanRAG, NodeRAG, GraphRAG, UniversalRAG) is built over TEXT entities/passages (or image/video); UniversalRAG explicitly has no audio; multimodal-KG systems (M3KG-RAG/MegaRAG/MDKAG) admit audio only after ASR transcription. Open question our system is first to test: do hierarchy/graph gains survive when keys are acoustic embeddings (content+speaker+emotion entangled) rather than clean text entities?

2. KG-family organization has a text precondition that conflicts with our cascade-free premise. GraphRAG/HippoRAG-2/LeanRAG/NodeRAG all require LLM TRIPLE/ENTITY EXTRACTION to build the store — which assumes text. For a speech KB you must either (a) ASR-then-extract (reintroduces the cascade our frozen-omni design avoids) or (b) extract entities directly from audio via the omni model (untested, no measurement anywhere). This is an unbenchmarked fork.

3. All measured wins are on TEXT QA benchmarks (2Wiki, MuSiQue, HotpotQA, QuALITY, NQ) read by a TEXT LLM. No paper measures whether a hierarchical/graph/grain-tagged organization still helps when the CONSUMER is a frozen OMNI model fed audio + retrieved context. Structure benefit for omni-model consumption is unestablished.

4. Grain-tagged hybrid store is asserted/converged (three-tier episodic/semantic/procedural taxonomy) but under-measured: almost no head-to-head of a grain-tagged hybrid vs a single-type flat store on the SAME task. Our own store could produce the first such measurement.

5. Build-cost numbers all assume API GPT-4-class LLMs ($10-15/800KB indexing; token counts). NONE quantify the offline build (recursive summarization / triple extraction) on a LOCAL llama.cpp 30B. Our wall-clock index-build cost is unknown and likely the binding constraint for adopting any LLM-summarization structure.

6. Organization vs retrieval-strategy is confounded in the headline results. HippoRAG-2's win = open-KG org PLUS Personalized-PageRank retrieval; it is not decomposed, so the measured gain cannot be attributed to organization alone. Our grid should separate value-org from retrieval-strategy (PathRAG-style pruning shows they ARE separable) to avoid crediting the wrong lever.

7. Write-back / consolidation policies (A-MEM neighbor-rewrite, mem0 ADD/UPDATE/DELETE, AutoDream idle-consolidation, SAGE novelty gate) are the obvious surface for our later training-free RL lever, but every one is heuristic or LLM-prompted today — none is optimized by an RL controller, and none is measured on speech-keyed memory. This is the clearest 'out-of-mock -> step-3 RL' opening.

8. Freshness/latency counter-evidence exists but is thin: GraphRAG -13.4% on NQ, -16.6% on time-sensitive, ~2.3x latency — but these come from secondary analyses/snippets not opened at source; the freshness penalty of structured org for a locally-served loop needs first-party verification before we let it govern a design choice."
